meaning: The action needs the admin role.
fix: Sign in as the admin user (the local desktop session is the admin). Settings pages that change configuration are admin-only.

meaning: AI features are switched off.
fix: Settings -> AI: turn AI on and pick a profile. Every other feature works without AI; the Copilot still answers from built-in documentation.

meaning: The configured model could not be reached.
fix: For a local model check that Ollama (or your llama.cpp server) is running and the model name exists (Tool Manager / Setup show it). For a cloud profile check the key and the network. The Copilot falls back to documentation-only answers meanwhile.

meaning: Offline mode is on, so network sources and downloads are denied.
fix: Settings -> turn Offline mode off. Local AI and stored cases keep working in offline mode.

meaning: Searches can only be run on an open case.
fix: Reopen the case, or create a new one.

meaning: Archived cases are read-only.
fix: Unarchive the case first if you need to add to it.

meaning: Policy refused the plan or request (for example offline mode, a closed case, a private/forbidden destination, or an unconfirmed active source). Nothing was started.
fix: Read the denial reason shown with it; it names the rule. Fix the cause (turn offline mode off, confirm the sources that need confirmation) and preview again.

meaning: Policy would currently block part of this workflow.
fix: Preview the workflow, read which step is blocked and why, then change the target or settings.

meaning: This is an explicit action and needs confirm=true (the UI sends it when you press the confirm button).
fix: Press the confirm button in the UI; nothing happens until you do.

meaning: You must tick that you own or are authorised to import the material.
fix: Tick the ownership/authorisation box on the Imports or Evidence tab before choosing a file.

meaning: Consent recorded for a human source has expired.
fix: Renew consent on the Humint tab before adding more material.

meaning: Consent for this source was withdrawn.
fix: No further material may be added or used for this source.

meaning: People/public-identity cases need a documented purpose.
fix: Write the purpose of the investigation when creating the case.

meaning: A real hardware receiver needs an ownership/authorisation assessment and your region.
fix: Complete the assessment on the Hardware tab, or use the simulated/replay device.

meaning: That hardware device is already recording.
fix: Stop the running capture on the Hardware tab first.

meaning: This case does not allow sending content to a cloud model.
fix: Use a local model, or change the case's AI policy on the AI tab (your decision, per case).

meaning: This case forbids sending RESTRICTED material to a cloud model.
fix: Use a local model or change the case policy.

meaning: A cited evidence item does not belong to this case.
fix: Cite evidence from the same case.

meaning: A claim with no evidence cannot be verified.
fix: Attach an evidence item to the claim first.

meaning: Accepting needs an evidence item from this case.
fix: Pick an evidence item first.

meaning: A claim needs an object entity or a value.
fix: Fill in the value or choose an entity.

meaning: That merge would be circular or self-referential.
fix: Pick two different entities that are not already merged into each other.

meaning: Entities of different types cannot be merged.
fix: Merge only entities of the same type.

meaning: These entities are already merged.
fix: Split the existing merge first if you want to change it.

meaning: An item with that name already exists.
fix: Choose another name.

meaning: That alias already exists in this case.
fix: Use a different alias.

meaning: The item does not exist (or you cannot access it).
fix: Reload the page; the item may have been deleted.

meaning: The upload exceeds the size limit.
fix: Use a smaller file, or trim the capture.

meaning: The upload was empty.
fix: Choose a file with content.

meaning: The file type could not be detected.
fix: Choose the type explicitly on the Imports tab; the message lists supported kinds.

meaning: A setting name or value is not allowed.
fix: Use a value the Settings page offers.

meaning: That AI profile type is not valid.
fix: Ollama and llama.cpp profiles are always local (loopback addresses); cloud profiles need an https URL.

meaning: The model is not in the setup catalog.
fix: Pick a model listed in Setup, or add your own profile in Settings -> AI.

meaning: No update server address is set.
fix: Settings -> Updates: enter the manifest address.

meaning: The update manifest is malformed or its signature does not match the key built into the app.
fix: Re-publish the manifest with the right key (scripts/update_tool.py publish). The key cannot be changed from the UI.

meaning: The downloaded update does not match the signed SHA-256 and was deleted.
fix: Re-publish the file and manifest together; never run a file that failed verification.

meaning: The update server name could not be resolved.
fix: Check the address and your network.

meaning: A network request failed (no route, refused, timed out).
fix: Check the network or the server address; the message names the exception type.

meaning: Report generation raised an error.
fix: Check the troubleshooting log for the exception, try another format (HTML/Markdown) and report the exception name.

meaning: The source needs an API key that is not stored.
fix: Setup -> API keys: paste the key and Save. Without one the source makes no request.

meaning: The source needs configuration before it can run.
fix: Read the warning on the run; for Amass this is data sources in its config file.

meaning: The tool is not installed.
fix: Setup: tick the tool and press Install selected, or install it yourself; then re-check in Tool Manager.

meaning: The source asked the app to slow down.
fix: Wait the stated time; the app never tries to evade rate limits. Try another source meanwhile.

meaning: The source did not answer in time.
fix: Retry later or use an alternative source for the same question.

meaning: This tool does not run on this operating system.
fix: Use an alternative (Tool Manager lists them) or run on a supported OS.

meaning: A plugin tried to reach a network address it did not declare.
fix: The plugin is blocked by design; review its manifest.

meaning: A plugin file changed after it was approved.
fix: It is disabled again; review the manifest and accept the new hash if you trust it.

meaning: A tool's output could not be parsed.
fix: The raw output was kept as evidence; check the tool version in Tool Manager.

meaning: No RDAP server is known for that TLD.
fix: Try a different registry source (crt.sh or DNS) for that domain.

meaning: DNS lookup failed.
fix: Check connectivity; the name may not exist.

meaning: A backup could not be created; the message gives the reason (for example a passphrase shorter than 8 characters).
fix: Use a passphrase of 8 or more characters and try again from Settings -> Encryption & backup.

meaning: A backup could not be restored (wrong passphrase, damaged file, or the target folder is not empty).
fix: Restore always writes into a new empty folder; check the passphrase and the file. The existing data folder is never modified.

meaning: Recurring monitoring of an individual needs a documented case purpose and an acknowledgement.
fix: Write the case purpose and tick the acknowledgement when creating the schedule.

meaning: The plugin package or its manifest is not valid.
fix: Check the manifest against the plugin SDK documentation and re-import.

meaning: The plugin action was refused (not reviewed, hash changed, or it asked for something not allowed).
fix: Review the manifest in Settings -> Plugins; a changed file disables the plugin until you accept the new hash.

meaning: The schedule definition is not valid.
fix: Choose a supported interval and a valid workflow.

meaning: The licence basis for this dataset does not permit importing it.
fix: Provide the licence basis and licensor the dataset allows, or do not import it.

meaning: The imported file could not be parsed.
fix: Check the file type and that the file is not damaged; the Imports tab lists supported kinds.

meaning: That tool is not on the installable list for this operating system.
fix: Open Setup to see what can be installed here, or install the tool yourself and re-check in Tool Manager.

meaning: The operating system credential store could not be used for a key.
fix: Unlock or install a credential store (on Linux a Secret Service such as gnome-keyring); without one the app seals keys in its encrypted database.

meaning: The workflow definition is not valid (bad reference, cycle, missing scope check, unknown setting, over a limit).
fix: Open the Checks panel: each problem names the step and the rule. Fix them, then publish.

meaning: A step names a source that is not registered in this installation.
fix: Pick a registered source (the editor lists them) or install the tool in Setup.

meaning: The target was refused by scope policy (private, local, unauthorised or malformed). It is never retried.
fix: Use a public target you are allowed to examine, or add a scope authorization for active collection; widening scope is your decision.

meaning: The scope authorization behind this run expired or was revoked.
fix: Renew the authorization, then request and grant the approval again.

meaning: An approval, confirmation or published version is missing or expired for this exact version.
fix: Publish, press Request approval, decide it (with an expiry), then activate or run again.

meaning: A source needs an API key or an approved destination that is not configured.
fix: Add the key in Setup -> API keys, or approve the webhook name in Automations -> Settings.

meaning: A source is not installed, is offline, or failed.
fix: Install or repair it in Setup, retry later, or use the diagnosis's suggested alternative.

meaning: The run was stopped.
fix: Start it again if you still want the result.

meaning: The run finished but some sources failed or were optional and unavailable.
fix: Open the run's warnings; results are marked partial and are not used as a baseline.

meaning: Offline mode is on, so network steps pause.
fix: Turn offline mode off, then retry the paused run.

meaning: The draft changed since you loaded it (someone or something saved a newer revision).
fix: Reload the workflow and re-apply your edit.
